summary: The storefront cache ages entries on a wall clock, so a backward step extends their real lifetime
description:
**Carried out of TKT-206's ai-review (pass 2) as the half of a finding that was deliberately not fixed there.**

`web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts` measures an entry's age from an injected `now()` that is `Date.now` in production — a **wall** clock. An NTP step backwards makes elapsed time negative.

**What TKT-206 fixed:** age is now a per-entry **high-water mark**, `max(previously reported, upstream + clamped elapsed)`. A live entry can no longer report a smaller age than a previous call already established, so the middleware cannot hand a page back freshness it had already spent. That was the part TKT-206 introduced, and it is closed.

**What remains open, and is this ticket:** after a backward step the age stops advancing until wall time catches up, so an entry can **outlive its TTL in real time by roughly the size of the jump**. A buyer can see an event listing that should have expired.

**Not a regression.** This cache measured wall time before TKT-206 touched it, and the reviewer checked the claim independently: *"It does not change expiry behavior, so the delayed-expiry residual genuinely predates TKT-206 and is not made worse by this patch."*

**Why it was not fixed there:** the fix changes the injected-clock contract. `PageDataCache`'s constructor takes `now: () => number` and that seam is shared with `web/storefront/src/middleware.ts` and every existing cache test, several of which drive wall-clock milliseconds directly. Swapping the source is a small change with a wide blast radius through test fixtures, and it deserves to be reviewed as itself rather than as a footnote to a 1,800-line caching ticket.

**Conditions of Success:**
- [ ] Entry aging uses a **monotonic** elapsed-time source (`performance.now()` in Node/SSR, or an injected monotonic clock), so a wall-clock step in either direction cannot change how long an entry lives.
- [ ] Expiry is bounded in real time: a test steps the clock backward mid-life and proves the entry still expires within its original budget.
- [ ] The high-water behaviour TKT-206 added is preserved — a monotonic source should make it redundant rather than contradict it. Say which, and if redundant, remove it rather than leaving two mechanisms for one property.
- [ ] The existing injected-clock tests keep working, or are migrated deliberately with the reason recorded. `middleware.ts` still derives outgoing `Cache-Control` from remaining freshness correctly.
- [ ] `make check` green, including the TS build (vitest does **not** typecheck — run the build before the full gate).

Quality gates: `make check`.

### ✅ Implementation readiness — PASS

All 8 items `met`.

**Shaping changed the ticket's own risk assessment.** It was filed with "a small change with a wide blast radius through test fixtures, several of which drive wall-clock milliseconds directly". Reading `web/storefront/test/cache.test.ts` does not support that: every case already constructs `new PageDataCache(fetchSpy, () => nowMs)` with a hand-driven counter. The injected seam is already universal, and forward-stepping counters already satisfy a monotonic contract. The change is the **default** plus **one** production construction (`api.ts:25`) — smaller than filed, and the drafter should not budget for a fixture migration that isn't there.

**Two traps written into `approach`/`success`:**
1. **Do not delete TKT-206's high-water mark** as newly redundant. It answers a different adversary (a shrinking upstream `Age` header, and a per-process monotonic clock behind a map that outlives neither cleanly). AGENTS.md's dead-mechanism rule cuts both ways — the test is "name an input where it changes the output", and here you can.
2. **Move both `ageOf()` call sites**, `get()` and `#sweep()`. Sweeping is what evicts; a fix that only corrects `get()` leaves the map growing on the wrong clock, and a test written against `get()` alone cannot see it — which is precisely why the class already exposes `size`.

The backward-step test must be shown **red at HEAD** before the fix.

### Execution plan — drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna` (codex `task`, effort high)

Per `config.models.plan`. Read-only run (no `--write`), job `task-mt99829s-0tj675`, 13,045 bytes,
conclusive. The run was hijacked by an unrelated local skill at startup (a `sed` of
`~/.ai/skills/r0/unslop/SKILL.md`, exit 2) — the documented, unpreventable shape; it returned
concrete code-cited findings anyway, so it is a PASS on `codex-runner.md`'s criterion.

**Briefed with** the ticket + COS, the shaping pass's two traps, the scope decision, governing ADRs
(ADR-004, ADR-006, ADR-045, each with what it constrains *for this ticket*), and governing tests
(`cache.test.ts`, `middleware-page-tier.test.ts`, the smoke suite's `X-Page-Data-Age`). Re-resolved
against `docs/adr/` at claim time, not taken from the shaping-time snapshot.

**Two things worth flagging before the critique reads it:**

1. It reaches the **opposite verdict** from the shaping note on the high-water mark — delete, not
   keep — and it argues the point rather than asserting it: `get()` deletes an expired entry
   (`cache.ts:155`) before the next fetch inserts a fresh `Entry` with a new `reportedAgeSeconds`,
   so the mark **never crosses a fetch boundary** and the "upstream Age shrinks between fetches"
   adversary the shaping note named is not one it can defend against. That is exactly the
   one-sentence input test AGENTS.md demands, run honestly and returning empty. The critique gets
   this as its primary target.
2. It found a **governing test my brief did not name**: `web/storefront/test/page-call-budget.test.ts`.
   Verified — it exists, and its `beforeEach` freezes `Date.now` with a 20-line comment explaining
   that the order is load-bearing (TKT-218, the commit immediately before HEAD). **If the cache
   stops reading `Date.now`, that freeze silently stops freezing anything** and the load-sensitivity
   flake TKT-218 closed reopens — as a test that passes while proving nothing, which is the failure
   mode that ticket's own comment says its first attempt hit. This is the single highest-value catch
   in the draft.

---

# TKT-212 execution plan

## DoD

- `PageDataCache` computes local elapsed time from a monotonic millisecond clock in both `get()` and `#sweep()`.
- Production construction in `web/storefront/src/lib/api.ts:25` uses the monotonic clock explicitly.
- `upstreamAgeSeconds`, `maxAgeSeconds`, and `CachedResult` retain their current semantics and types.
- A regression test is red at HEAD when `Date.now()` steps backward, then green with the monotonic implementation.
- The regression test proves eviction through `cache.size`, not only through a re-fetch.
- TKT-206's non-decreasing age behavior remains observable without retaining a redundant high-water field.
- Existing forward-only injected-clock tests continue to pass after the callback is renamed to reflect monotonic semantics.
- `page-call-budget.test.ts` freezes `performance.now()` before importing the production singleton.
- Middleware continues publishing remaining freshness, including `Cache-Control: ... max-age=1` for age 299 of 300.
- The storefront TypeScript build and `make check` pass.

## Design decision on the clock seam

Use one injected clock, repurposing the existing `now` callback as the monotonic elapsed-time source.

In `cache.ts`:

- Rename `#now` and local variables such as `nowMs` to `#monotonicNow` and `monotonicNowMs`.
- Change the constructor default at current line 96 from `Date.now` to a wrapper around `performance.now()`.
- Keep `fetchedAtMs` in milliseconds. Its value becomes monotonic-clock time, not epoch time.
- Pass monotonic values to both current `ageOf()` call sites:
  - `#sweep()` at current lines 122-127.
  - `get()` at current lines 131-150.
- Keep `upstreamAgeSeconds` unchanged. ADR-045 makes clear that only the local elapsed term belongs to this ticket.

At the production construction site, `api.ts:25` should pass the same monotonic helper explicitly. This makes the only production cache owner visibly bound to the intended clock while preserving a monotonic default for other callers and tests.

Do not add a wall-clock callback. The cache has no reason to read wall time. The regression test will control two independent clocks outside the cache:

- `performance.now()`, representing elapsed real time and advancing monotonically.
- `Date.now()`, representing the hostile wall clock that steps backward.

The test must construct `new PageDataCache(fetchSpy)` without an injected callback. It should spy on both clocks before construction, because the constructor stores the resolved default callback.

Rejected alternatives:

- Injecting one clock and stepping it backward tests an invalid monotonic source, not the defect.
- Injecting separate wall and monotonic clocks into the cache adds a dependency the implementation does not need and permits the cache to accidentally consult the wrong one.
- Stubbing only `Date.now()` after construction misses the captured default callback and can produce a green test that proves nothing.
- Sleeping in the test measures scheduler behavior and makes the result flaky. Deterministic `performance.now()` values model elapsed real time directly.

## Verdict on the high-water mark

Delete `reportedAgeSeconds` and the `Math.max()` high-water calculation.

The high-water mark is redundant once the source is monotonic for this implementation:

```text
upstreamAgeSeconds + floor((monotonicNowMs - fetchedAtMs) / 1000)
```

For one `Entry`, `upstreamAgeSeconds` and `fetchedAtMs` are fixed. A monotonic clock makes the local term non-decreasing, so the expression cannot report a smaller age.

The shaping note's proposed “upstream Age shrinks between fetches” case is not covered by the current high-water field. When `get()` expires an entry, line 155 deletes it. The next fetch creates a new `Entry` at line 192 with a new `reportedAgeSeconds` value. The mark does not cross fetches. A process restart also loses the map, so the mark cannot protect entries across process lifetimes.

Therefore, the input class where the high-water field changes output while the clock contract is valid is empty. If upstream age regression across separate fetches becomes a requirement, it needs a cross-entry policy, not this per-entry field.

The current TKT-206 behavior remains guaranteed by the monotonic source. Keep the `describe('age is monotonic under a backward clock')` coverage, but migrate it to drive `performance.now()` forward while moving `Date.now()` backward. Do not keep tests that step the injected monotonic callback backward.

Before finalizing the deletion, perform the deliberate mutation of removing the high-water expression. The migrated age tests should stay green. That green result is the evidence that the mechanism no longer changes output under its valid inputs.

## Files to touch

- `web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts`
  - Add the monotonic clock helper.
  - Change the constructor default from `Date.now` to `performance.now()`.
  - Rename the clock field and local variables to make the contract explicit.
  - Use the monotonic value in both `get()` and `#sweep()`.
  - Remove `reportedAgeSeconds` from `Entry`.
  - Remove the high-water update in `get()`.
  - Update comments that currently describe the clock as a wall clock.

- `web/storefront/src/lib/api.ts:25`
  - Bind the sole production `PageDataCache` instance explicitly to the monotonic helper.

- `web/storefront/test/cache.test.ts`
  - Rename forward-only fixture clocks to monotonic-clock terminology.
  - Replace the current backward-injected-clock cases around lines 301-347 with independent wall/monotonic clock tests.
  - Add the sweep regression that asserts `cache.size`.
  - Preserve the upstream-age and combined-age tests around lines 170-234.

- `web/storefront/test/page-call-budget.test.ts`
  - Freeze `performance.now()` instead of only `Date.now()` in the `beforeEach` around lines 123-126.
  - Update comments that currently describe the cache as wall-clock based.

No changes are needed in `middleware.ts` or `page-tier.ts`. Their existing behavior is the required consumer contract. `middleware-page-tier.test.ts` should remain unchanged and run as a regression check.

## Test plan

### 1. `uses the default monotonic clock when the wall clock rolls backward`

Location: replace the first case in `describe('age is monotonic under a backward clock')`, currently around `cache.test.ts:302`.

Setup:

- Spy on `performance.now()` and `Date.now()` before constructing the cache.
- Return `1_000` from `performance.now()` and `10_000_000` from `Date.now()`.
- Construct `new PageDataCache(fetchSpy)`, with no clock override.
- Fetch a response with `max-age=10`.
- Advance `performance.now()` to `6_000`.
- Move `Date.now()` backward to `9_995_000`.
- Read the same URL.

Assertions:

- The fetch spy was called once.
- The result reports `ageSeconds === 5`.
- The entry remains live.

Why it is red at HEAD: the constructor captures `Date.now` at current line 96, so the backward wall step makes the local elapsed term zero. The test expects the five seconds represented by the monotonic clock.

Mutation checks:

- Change the constructor default back to `Date.now`. The age assertion fails.
- Change only the `get()` clock read to `Date.now`. The age assertion fails.
- Remove the new test's wall-clock manipulation. This checks that the test is actually observing the independent clocks rather than merely testing elapsed time.

### 2. `sweeps an entry after monotonic TTL elapsed despite a wall-clock rollback`

Location: add under `describe('expired entries are swept')`, near current `cache.test.ts:243`.

Setup:

- Spy on both clocks before constructing `new PageDataCache(fetchSpy)`.
- Fetch `/entry` at monotonic time `1_000` and wall time `10_000_000`.
- Use `max-age=10`.
- Move the wall clock backward to `9_995_000`.
- Move the monotonic clock to `12_000`, representing 11 seconds since insertion.
- Request `/other` to trigger insertion and therefore `#sweep()`.

Assertions:

- `cache.size` is `1`.
- The remaining entry is `/other`, established by a fetch spy or distinct response payload.

Why it is red at HEAD: HEAD's `#sweep()` receives `Date.now()`, which is still behind the insertion time, so `/entry` appears live and the map grows to two entries. The monotonic implementation sees 11 seconds against a 10-second TTL and removes it before inserting `/other`.

Mutation checks:

- Change only `#sweep()` to use `Date.now()`. The size assertion becomes `2`.
- Delete the `#sweep()` call from `#fetchThrough()`. The size assertion becomes `2`.
- Change only `get()` to use `Date.now()`. Test 1 fails while this test may still pass, proving the two call sites have separate coverage.

### 3. Existing upstream-age tests

Location: `cache.test.ts:170-234`.

Keep these tests and rename their hand-driven callback variables to monotonic terminology. Their counters already move forward, so no fixture migration is required.

Retain these assertions:

- A miss reports the upstream `Age`.
- Local monotonic elapsed time is added to upstream age.
- Expiry uses combined upstream plus local age.
- Already-expired responses are not retained.

Mutation checks:

- Remove `upstreamAgeSeconds` from the age calculation. The combined-age and expiry tests fail.
- Seed entries at local age zero. The upstream-age propagation tests fail.
- Change expiry to use only local elapsed time. The near-expiry upstream-age test fails.

### 4. TKT-206 non-regression coverage

Location: the existing `describe('age is monotonic under a backward clock')` block.

Keep the block and rewrite its fixtures so `performance.now()` never moves backward. Move only `Date.now()` backward. This preserves the observable TKT-206 contract without testing an invalid injected monotonic source.

A case that first advances the monotonic clock, then rolls back the wall clock, should assert that the reported age does not decrease. This test may remain green at HEAD because the existing high-water mark masks the wall-clock defect. That is acceptable for a non-regression test. Test 1 is the required red-at-HEAD coverage.

Mutation check:

- Remove the high-water field and expression. The migrated test should remain green. This confirms the monotonic source, rather than the deleted field, supplies the guarantee.

### 5. Middleware remaining-freshness regression

Location: existing `middleware-page-tier.test.ts:28-32`.

Keep the current assertion that age 299 of max age 300 produces:

```text
public, max-age=1, s-maxage=1
```

Mutation checks:

- Replace remaining freshness with the full max age. The test fails.
- Remove `ageSeconds` from the result passed to the middleware. The test fails.

### 6. SSR page-call budget

Location: `page-call-budget.test.ts:99-129`.

Change the fixture to freeze `performance.now()` before dynamically importing `api.ts`, because the production singleton will now use the monotonic clock.

Keep the existing page rendering and one-upstream-call assertions. This test verifies that the production construction site and module-level singleton remain deterministic under the new default.

Mutation check:

- Restore the real `performance.now()` in the fixture. The test can become scheduler-sensitive and should no longer provide the intended deterministic guarantee.

## Risks and failure modes

- A test that injects one callback and steps that callback backward is tautological. It can pass while production still uses `Date.now()`.
- Stubbing `Date.now()` after constructing the cache misses the captured default callback. Stub before construction, as the existing page-call-budget test already documents for `Date.now()`.
- A test that calls `get()` after expiry does not prove eviction. The cache re-fetches even if the old map entry was never deleted. The sweep test must request a different URL and assert `cache.size`.
- If the test advances the wall clock before rolling it backward, TKT-206's current high-water mark can mask the defect. The required red test rolls the wall clock backward before any call establishes a larger reported age.
- Changing `get()` but not `#sweep()` leaves stale entries in the map. The separate `size` assertion catches this.
- Changing `#sweep()` but not `get()` leaves middleware age reporting on the wrong clock. Test 1 catches this.
- `performance.now()` is relative milliseconds, not epoch milliseconds. Do not serialize it, compare it with HTTP dates, or alter `CachedResult`.
- Do not alter `upstreamAgeSeconds` or `parseAge()`. ADR-045 assigns that value to catalog's wire-level cache age.
- A real-time sleep would make the test slow and flaky. Use controlled monotonic values.
- A production default that directly stores an unbound `performance.now` method may be runtime-sensitive. Use a wrapper helper and reuse that helper at `api.ts:25`.
- No ADR change is required. The implementation stays within ADR-004 and ADR-006, and ADR-045's upstream/local age split remains intact.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan-final -->
### Plan critique + finalization — `main-agent` (per `config.models.planReview`)

Cross-model check: `plan` = `gpt-5.6-luna`, `planReview` = `main-agent`. Distinct. Every file,
symbol and line number the draft names was verified to exist at HEAD (f75d73f4) with `sed -n` /
`git grep -n`, not taken on trust.

**The kind=plan draft as amended below is the plan.** Delta only.

---

#### A1 — ACCEPT the high-water deletion, and reject the shaping note that said to keep it

The draft reached the *opposite* verdict from shaping, and it is right. I proved it rather than
preferring it. Within one `Entry` the fields fixed at insert are `U = upstreamAgeSeconds` and
`F = fetchedAtMs`; `R = reportedAgeSeconds` starts at `U` and is only ever assigned a previous
`ageOf()`. With a monotonic `t`, `U + elapsed(t)` is non-decreasing, and by induction
`R <= U + elapsed(t)` at every call — so `max(R, U + elapsed(t))` collapses to `U + elapsed(t)`.
**The `max()` term is inert.** Across entries it cannot help either: `get()` deletes the expired
entry (`cache.ts:155`) and `#fetchThrough` inserts a fresh one with `reportedAgeSeconds:
upstreamAgeSeconds` (`cache.ts:196`), so `R` never crosses a fetch boundary and the "upstream `Age`
shrinks between fetches" adversary the shaping note named is one this mechanism structurally cannot
defend against.

That is AGENTS.md's *"the mechanism was inert, not the test"* rule (TKT-162) run exactly as written:
I can state no input for which it changes the output. It goes.

**Independent confirmation the draft did not have, and it is strong.** `web/storefront/src/lib/session.ts:129-154`
already solved this identical problem in this same package under **TKT-220**, and its comment records:
*"A first attempt at this fix clamped `Date.now()` to a non-decreasing floor. That does not work, and
the mutation check is what showed it."* A non-decreasing floor **is** the high-water mark. A sibling
module already learned by mutation that this exact mechanism is the wrong tool for this exact defect.
Keeping it would leave two mechanisms for one property with the dead one reading as a guarantee —
precisely what AGENTS.md says to delete.

**Amendment:** adopt `session.ts`'s `monotonicNow()` idiom and *name TKT-220 in the comment*. This is
not a new pattern in the storefront; it is the second application of an established one.

#### A2 — ACCEPT the `page-call-budget.test.ts` catch. This is the plan's most valuable finding.

Verified. `test/page-call-budget.test.ts:125` does `vi.spyOn(Date, 'now').mockReturnValue(FROZEN_NOW_MS)`
under a 20-line comment (TKT-218, the commit immediately before HEAD) explaining that the freeze stops
machine load from reading as a page-call-budget violation, and that **the spy must be installed before
the first import** because the singleton binds the resolved default.

The moment the cache stops reading `Date.now`, **that freeze silently stops freezing anything** and
TKT-218's flake reopens — as a green test that proves nothing, which that ticket's own comment says
its first attempt hit. My brief never named this file; the drafter found it. Freezing `performance.now`
in that `beforeEach`, in the same before-import position, is **required, not optional**, and the
comment must be updated to say the cache is monotonic now.

#### A3 — AMEND Test 1: as drafted it cannot distinguish "expires on monotonic" from "never expires"

The one place I disagree with the draft on substance, and it is the shape TKT-220's review needed
**three passes** to find. Draft Test 1 asserts `ageSeconds === 5`, one fetch call, and a *live* entry.
It is genuinely red at HEAD (`Date` steps back 5s → `elapsed` clamps to 0 → `ageOf` reports 0, not 5)
and it does catch the default being reverted. But every assertion is about an entry that is **alive**;
nothing in it observes the TTL boundary. An implementation that never expires anything passes it.
Draft Test 2 covers eviction, but on a different URL and a different entry, so nothing asserts that
the monotonic clock **ends this entry's life**.

`session.test.ts:332-355` is the worked answer and its comment enumerates all three unfalsifiable
shapes it went through. **Amendment — Test 1 gains a third leg, asserting both halves in one
sequence:** after the backward-step assertions, advance `performance.now()` past `max-age` **while
`Date.now` stays rolled back**, and assert a re-fetch (`fetchSpy` called twice). Nothing in that leg
can be attributed to the wall clock, because the wall clock is still behind where it started.

#### A4 — AMEND: do not pass the clock explicitly at `api.ts:25`

The draft wants `api.ts:25` to bind the monotonic helper explicitly "so the production owner is
visibly bound to the intended clock". **Reject.** It defeats A2 and Test 1 at once: both depend on
the production singleton exercising the *default* argument, and TKT-220's third listed failure was
exactly *"injecting `now` ANYWHERE means the production clock default is never exercised, so swapping
`monotonicNow` back to `Date.now` would leave the test green"*. An explicit binding at the only
production site means the default is unexercised in production and every mutation of it survives.
Leave `new PageDataCache()` bare; the default is the thing under test. Visibility is a comment's job.

#### A5 — CONFIRM, no change: the gateway smoke suite is a real end-to-end guard here

`smoke/catalog_publication_test.go:347-358` sleeps 2 real seconds and requires `X-Page-Data-Age >= 1`
with remaining `Cache-Control` strictly between 0 and 300. `performance.now()` measures real elapsed
in-process time, so this keeps passing — and it independently pins that the new clock still advances
in real time. Worth stating because "monotonic" could be mis-implemented as "frozen", and this catches
that in the real SSR process.

#### A6 — ACCEPT as drafted

DoD; the one-clock seam with `now` repurposed to monotonic (rejecting a second injected seam, which
would let the cache consult the wrong clock); both `ageOf()` call sites moving together; `#sweep`
proved through `size` on a second URL; `upstreamAgeSeconds` / `parseAge` / `CachedResult` untouched
per ADR-045; no middleware or `page-tier` change; no ADR needed.

---

### Decisions taken by the agent at Gate 2 (`config.gates: autonomous`)

Per § Autonomous mode: open decisions resolved by me, preferring the critique's recommendation, else
the most reversible option.

1. **High-water mark: DELETE** (draft's verdict over the shaping note's). Rationale in A1 — a proof
   of inertness plus a sibling module that learned the same thing by mutation. Reversible: it is a
   field and a `Math.max`, restorable in one commit if a real input class ever appears.
2. **One clock seam, `now` repurposed to monotonic** — not a second injected clock. Fewer ways to
   consult the wrong clock.
3. **No explicit clock at `api.ts:25`** (A4) — overrides the draft, on the stronger of the two
   arguments: an exercised default beats a visible one.
4. **`risk:low` remains NOT claimed**, as at claim time. Blast radius stayed small, but the fixture
   question was real and this critique changed the plan in three places.

### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

Per the skill's required section — design elements *added* here rather than accepted/amended from the
draft, which therefore reach Gate 2 reviewed only by their author (me):

1. **A3's third leg on Test 1** (advance monotonic past TTL while the wall clock stays rolled back).
   New test structure, not in the draft. Derived from `session.test.ts:332`, so it is a transplant of
   a reviewed pattern rather than an invention — but the transplant itself is unreviewed.
2. **A4's reversal** of the draft's `api.ts:25` recommendation. I am overruling the only model that
   reviewed this plan, on this point.

### Implementation — `main-agent` (per `config.models.implement`)

PR: https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/321 · branch `TKT-212-monotonic-cache-clock`
· commit `83e812ea` · diff **+171 / −87 (3 files)**.

```yaml

gate_result: EXIT=0, 75,371-byte log, no failure markers

tests: 203/203 storefront
files: web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts, test/cache.test.ts, test/page-call-budget.test.ts
```

#### TDD — the gap was demonstrated before it was closed

Both new tests were written first and **observed red at HEAD**: `ageSeconds` reported `0` where the
test expects `5`, and `cache.size` was `2` where the test expects `1`. That is the run AGENTS.md
requires of a ticket whose deliverable is coverage for an existing gap.

#### Mutation results — each run in ISOLATION

Deliberate, because a mutation caught by a pre-existing suite proves the mechanism is live, not that
the new test caught it. `-t` was used to run one case at a time.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| constructor default → `Date.now` | red |
| `get()` reads the wall clock | red |
| `#sweep()` reads the wall clock | red — **only after a fixture fix, see below** |
| entries never expire (`if (true)`) | red — caught by the A3 leg |
| `performance.now` freeze removed from `page-call-budget` | survives; verified another way, see below |

#### A fixture that could not fail, caught and fixed mid-run

**The first version of the sweep test passed under a wall-clock sweep.** With `Date.now` mocked at an
epoch value (~10 trillion) and `fetchedAtMs` holding a monotonic reading (1,000), a sweep on the wrong
clock computes a colossal elapsed and evicts the entry **anyway** — the right answer for the wrong
reason, so the mutation survived while the test looked like it covered the sweep.

Fixed by pinning the wall clock *near* the monotonic reading (`Date.now = () => 1_000`, then `500`),
so a wall-clock sweep sees `elapsed <= 0` and strands the entry. Re-verified green on correct code and
red under the mutation, in isolation. Noted here rather than quietly repaired: this is exactly
AGENTS.md's fixture-that-cannot-reach-the-failing-state, and it survived my own review of the test I
had just written.

#### A2 verified by simulation, since it cannot fail on demand

Removing the `performance.now` freeze from `page-call-budget.test.ts` leaves the suite green — expected,
because the freeze guards against a **slow** machine and a fast one never triggers it. Rather than
accept a surviving mutation, I simulated the condition: advancing the monotonic clock 400s between
reads makes `a repeat render inside the tier spends zero` fail. The freeze is live, and it now covers
the clock the cache actually reads. Freezing only `Date.now`, as HEAD does, would have left this
unguarded — the plan draft's catch, and it held up.

#### Plan adherence

All four Gate-2 decisions implemented as written: high-water mark deleted (A1), one repurposed clock
seam, **no explicit clock at `api.ts:25`** (A4 — the file is unmodified, which is the point: the
default is what the tests exercise), and `monotonicNow()` adopted from `session.ts` with TKT-220 cited
in the comment.

`upstreamAgeSeconds`, `parseAge`, `CachedResult`, `middleware.ts` and `page-tier.ts` untouched, per
ADR-045 and the scope decision. No ADR needed — the change is an application of ADR-004/006/045, not
a deviation.

**Deliberately NOT done:** `git add -A`. The three edited paths were staged by name (AGENTS.md, TKT-237).

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
### Adversarial review — `gpt-5.6-luna` (codex `adversarial-review`, per `config.models.aiReview`)

Cross-model check: `implement` = `main-agent`, `aiReview` = `gpt-5.6-luna`. Distinct.
Scope `--base origin/main --scope branch`, diff only — the plan and the reasoning were deliberately
withheld. Artifact 3,885 bytes, verdict `needs-attention`, conclusive. Skill hijack present again
(`~/.ai/skills/review/SKILL.md`); it returned code-cited findings regardless, so it is a PASS.

Primed for guilt across six named attack lines, not "check whether it's ok".

#### Finding 1 — [medium] "Removing the high-water mark breaks callers that inject a wall clock" (`cache.ts:110-121`)
**Verdict: PARTIALLY ACCEPTED — real as an unstated contract, rejected as a behavioural defect. Fixed
by documenting, not by restoring the mark.**

Verified against the revision under review, not the base. The mechanism the reviewer describes is
real: `now: () => number` accepts any callable, `ageOf` now trusts it not to move backwards, and a
caller passing `Date.now` would see a shrinking age.

But the caller is hypothetical. `git grep 'new PageDataCache('` across `web/storefront` returns **one
production site — `api.ts:25`, which passes nothing** — and ~20 test sites. The class is not exported
beyond the storefront package.

Two reasons the recommended fixes are both wrong here:

- *"Restore the age floor for untrusted clocks"* is the **validate-it answer to a make-it-unsubmittable
  problem** (AGENTS.md, TKT-244). A floor over a wall clock is precisely what TKT-206 shipped and what
  this ticket replaced, and `session.ts:143` records TKT-220 learning **by mutation** that it does not
  work. Re-adding it would restore an inert mechanism that reads as a guarantee.
- *"Separate the production path from test injection"* would defeat the tests. Injecting a clock
  anywhere in production means the default is never exercised, so swapping it back to `Date.now`
  leaves the whole suite green — TKT-220's third listed failure, and the reason A4 rejected the plan
  draft's `api.ts:25` binding.

`session.ts` faced the identical tension and shipped `now = monotonicNow()` — a defaulted, injectable,
documented-as-monotonic parameter — after three review passes. This diff now matches that precedent
explicitly: the contract is stated at `#now`, with what breaks if violated, why no production caller
passes it, and the TKT-220 citation. Commit `33639fa1`.

#### The five attack lines the reviewer did not report on — verified by me, labelled as my own work
It reported one finding of six requested angles. Rather than read silence as clearance, I checked the
rest myself:

- **(2) epoch mixing.** Clean. `fetchedAtMs` appears at `cache.ts:41`, `102`, `222` only, and is
  exclusively differenced against another reading of the same clock. Never serialized, never compared
  to an HTTP date. `CachedResult` carries *seconds of age*, not timestamps, so nothing relative
  escapes the class.
- **(3) can the two call sites disagree?** No. `get()` (`:179`) and `#sweep()` (`:163`) both route
  through the single `ageOf`, each fed from `this.#now()` (`:171`, `:219`). One definition of expiry,
  which is why `ageOf` was extracted.
- **(4) can a new test pass against a broken implementation?** **Yes — one did, and I found and fixed
  it during implementation, before this review.** Documented in the `kind=coding` comment: the sweep
  fixture mocked `Date.now` at an epoch value against a monotonic `fetchedAtMs`, so a wrong-clock
  sweep evicted anyway. Now pinned near the monotonic reading; re-verified red under the mutation in
  isolation. This was the reviewer's sharpest question and the answer was already on the board.
- **(5) freeze order/position.** Correct — both spies sit inside the same `beforeEach`, after
  `vi.resetModules()` and before the dynamic import, which is the load-bearing ordering TKT-218
  documents. Nothing else in that file needs real elapsed time.
- **(6) outside assumptions.** One found: a stale comment at `page-call-budget.test.ts:173` still
  describing the cache as wall-clock based. Corrected in `33639fa1`. `middleware.ts`, `page-tier.ts`
  and `env.d.ts` consume only `ageSeconds`/`maxAgeSeconds` and are clock-agnostic.

#### Second pass: NOT run — the fixes are trivial
Per the Hard rules. The fix diff is **comments only** — a doc block on `#now` and one corrected
comment. No control flow, no signature, no schema, no logic, no new or rewritten test; nothing a
second adversarial pass could attack that the first did not already see. Recorded here as the rule
requires, either way.

Gate re-run on the committed tree after the fixes: `EXIT=0`, 74,985-byte log, no failure markers.
203/203 storefront tests, TS build clean.

#### Triage summary
| finding | severity | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| high-water removal vs injected wall clocks | medium | partially accepted — contract documented at the seam; restoring the mark rejected with reasons |

No incidental findings, so no backlog tickets spawned. No blocking finding survives.

### Validation — each COS against evidence on the MERGED code

Merged as `dfd63373` (squash of PR #321). Verified on `origin/main` by content, not by the PR badge:
`git grep -c monotonicNow origin/main -- web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts` → 5, and
`reportedAgeSeconds` → **absent**. Post-merge `make check` on `main`: `EXIT=0`, 77,420-byte log, no
failure markers.

| # | Condition of Success | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Entry aging uses a monotonic elapsed-time source | **met** | `monotonicNow()` wraps `performance.now()`; constructor default is `monotonicNow`. Mutation: reverting the default to `Date.now` turns the new tests red. |
| 2 | Expiry bounded in real time; a test steps the clock backward mid-life and proves the entry still expires within its original budget | **met** | `ages on the default monotonic clock, which the wall clock cannot move OR extend` — the wall clock steps back 5s and the entry still reports age 5, then the monotonic clock crosses `max-age` **with the wall clock still rolled back** and the entry re-fetches. Both halves in one sequence. |
| 3 | The high-water mark is preserved OR removed with a stated verdict — not two mechanisms for one property | **met — removed, with the argument** | Under a monotonic source `max(reported, upstream + elapsed)` collapses to `upstream + elapsed` for every input; across entries the mark never crosses a fetch boundary because `get()` deletes the entry first. `session.ts:143` records TKT-220 learning by mutation that this shape is the wrong tool here. |
| 4 | Existing injected-clock tests keep working or are migrated deliberately; `middleware.ts` still derives outgoing `Cache-Control` from remaining freshness | **met** | 203/203 storefront tests. The ~19 pre-existing clock-injected cases are unchanged — their counters already stepped forward, so no migration was owed. `middleware.ts` and `page-tier.ts` are untouched and `middleware-page-tier.test.ts` passes unmodified. |
| 5 | `make check` green including the TS build (run the build before the gate) | **met** | TS build run first and clean, then the gate — green three times: pre-push, post-review-fix, post-merge on `main`. CI `check` + `gate-selftest` + `changes` + `repository-scan` all pass on the PR. |

#### What a buyer gets that they did not have before
An event listing served from the storefront's SSR cache now expires after **exactly its `max-age` of
real time**, whatever the host clock does. Before this, an NTP step backwards of *N* seconds extended
every live entry's real lifetime by roughly *N* — a listing that should have expired kept being served,
and the page's outgoing `Cache-Control` kept advertising freshness the data no longer had.

Not user-demonstrable through the UI (it needs a clock step on the SSR host), so it is validated
through code and tests, per the pipeline's rule for non-demonstrable COS. The end-to-end guard that
*is* real: `smoke/catalog_publication_test.go:347-358` sleeps 2 real seconds and requires
`X-Page-Data-Age >= 1` with remaining freshness strictly between 0 and 300 — it passes, which
independently confirms the new clock still advances in real time in the actual SSR process. That
matters because "monotonic" mis-implemented as "frozen" would satisfy every unit test in the diff.

#### Residual risk, stated plainly
`PageDataCache`'s `now` parameter still accepts any callable. Nothing enforces monotonicity at the
type level; the contract is documented at the seam (`cache.ts` `#now`) rather than made unrepresentable.
That is the same shape `session.ts` ships after three review passes, and every injection in the tree is
a test — but it is the one place a future caller could reintroduce the defect, so it is written down
here rather than left in the diff.

#### learnings:

objective.note: After a backward NTP step the storefront cache's age stops advancing until wall time catches up, so an entry outlives its TTL in real time by roughly the size of the jump and a buyer can be served an event listing that should have expired. TKT-206 closed the other half (age can no longer DECREASE); this is the residual its own code comment names.

scope.note: IN: web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts — the clock source behind entry aging and the #sweep, its default in the constructor, and the one production construction site. OUT: the high-water mark TKT-206 added (keep it — see approach), the upstream-age accounting, the in-flight coalescing, and ADR-004's cache tiers. No API or contract change.

uncertainties.note: Resolved by reading rather than deferred. The ticket predicted 'a wide blast radius through test fixtures'; that is NOT what the code shows. The injected-clock seam ALREADY exists — `constructor(fetchImpl, now: () => number = Date.now)` — and web/storefront/test/cache.test.ts drives every one of its ~19 cases through that injected `now`, never through the real clock. So the fixtures do not need rewriting: they are already clock-injected, and a monotonic contract is satisfied by the forward-stepping counters they already use. The real change is narrower than filed: the DEFAULT, plus the single production construction at web/storefront/src/lib/api.ts:25. Remaining unknown, and it is small: `performance.now()` in the Astro/Node SSR runtime returns ms since process start with sub-ms resolution — cheap to confirm with one node -e.

dependencies.note: None. No blockers, no links. TKT-206 is Done and is the reason the high-water mark exists.

approach.note: Swap the aging clock to a monotonic source (`performance.now()`, still injectable) and keep TKT-206's high-water mark rather than replacing it. **Keep it deliberately, and say so in the code**: the two mechanisms answer different adversaries — monotonic time closes the wall-clock STEP, the high-water mark closes an entry reporting less age than a previous call already established, which also covers a monotonic source that is per-process while the map is not. Deleting it as 'now redundant' is the tempting move and it is the AGENTS.md dead-mechanism trap run in reverse: before removing it, state in one sentence an input for which it changes the output — if you can (and you can: an upstream `Age` header that shrinks between fetches), it stays. Both `ageOf()` call sites must move together — `get()` AND `#sweep()`, which is the one that actually evicts.

first_slice.note: The whole ticket is one slice: one clock source, one default, one production call site, two tests. Nothing here is worth splitting.

success.note: The COS on the ticket, with one sharpened. A test that steps the injected clock BACKWARD mid-life and asserts the entry still expires within its original real-time TTL is the ticket's proof — and it must be shown RED against HEAD before the fix, or it is a test about the new code rather than about the defect (AGENTS.md: a coverage ticket must demonstrate its gap). Second assertion, easy to omit: prove eviction, not just re-fetch. `#sweep` is the path that frees memory, and `get()` re-fetches an expired entry whether or not it was ever dropped — the existing suite already exposes `size` for exactly this reason, so assert on `size`.

context_memo.note: governingAdrs: ADR-004 (docs/adr/ADR-004-cache-first-read-path.md) — the cache-first read path and its tiers, incl. the TKT-128 amendment noting no CDN or shared cache exists anywhere in the stack, which is what bounds this defect's blast radius to the SSR process's own map. Resolves at HEAD. governingTests: web/storefront/test/cache.test.ts — ~19 cases, all clock-injected, and the file that will prove or fail to prove this; note its TKT-206 block (`:166+`) which pins the high-water behaviour that must SURVIVE this change. Also web/storefront/src/lib/api.ts:25, the single production construction site — not a test, but the one line where the default actually takes effect.
